newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits rise 2.1 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits rise 2.1 pct in October.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in October rose 2.1 percent to C$2.12 billion, seasonally adjusted, from September, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Oct Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 2.2 percent after a 3.4 percent fall in September.
Statistics Canada said the sharp increase in residential building permits was due to "exceptionally" low mortgage rates and an upbeat housing resale market.

"The advance suggests the affordability of housing is offsetting lukewarm consumer confidence, which took a slight dip in the third quarter, according to a Conference Board of Canada survey," the government agency said.
The value of non-residential building permits fell for the third month in a row.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labor and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
